title: Exact count matching left no clear detection-rate difference for one-map and two-map worm connections
abstract: We tested whether chemical connections present in two adult worm maps have higher evoked-response detection rates at the same synapse count. This follows a prior campaign prediction test. Exact count matching retained 545 of 1397 measured connected pairs in six count strata. The overlap-weighted rate difference was -0.44 percentage points, with a conditional 95 percent shared-cell bootstrap interval of -12.31 to 10.91 points. Matching source identity and count retained 226 pairs; matching target identity and count retained 168 pairs. Both intervals also crossed zero. A separate ridge prediction check and seven sensitivity checks gave no clear added gain. These results do not establish equal function. Two anatomical animals, different functional animals, low event counts, poor count overlap and conditional uncertainty limit the test. New code, aggregate evidence, figures, exact input hashes and external retrieval steps support reproduction. External records are not bundled.
